headline: High: shared MCP and broad egress create default data-leak and action-conflict risks; prompt-injection and cascading errors are also plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP surfaces, so content from next-ai-draw-io can reach OpenMetadata through a shared protocol channel. next-ai-draw-io also uses natural-language commands and browser-assisted workflows, which increases the chance that untrusted diagram or document text is treated as instructions. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io passes document text into MCP tool calls without provenance tagging
IF OpenMetadata consumes MCP payloads as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable MCP bridging between the two agents
Require provenance labels on all cross-agent text
Strip instruction-like prefixes from imported documents
Review one sample workflow for prompt-injection markers
requires-engineering: add allowlisted tool schemas

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, images, diagrams, and API keys, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory data and can call APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. A shared workspace or MCP path could move sensitive document contents into OpenMetadata or send metadata back out through broad egress. Because both agents have networked surfaces and the pairwise isolation is undocumented, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same workspace or MCP endpoint
IF PDFs, images, or API keys from next-ai-draw-io are ingested into OpenMetadata
IF OpenMetadata forwards catalog or lineage data to external APIs or webhooks
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials immediately
Disable webhook/API egress for shared runs
Move secrets out of any shared directory
Test one benign file transfer path end-to-end
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent ACLs on shared storage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both profiles support multiple instances and both can write through networked or MCP-mediated workflows, so concurrent updates to shared mutable resources are plausible. next-ai-draw-io can manipulate files and diagrams, while OpenMetadata can mutate catalog state via APIs and webhooks. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so overlapping writes are a default-risk medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same shared directory or metadata backend
IF either agent performs writes without external locking
IF concurrent runs are enabled in the orchestrator
mitigations: Run the agents in separate namespaces
Pause one agent during writes
Use a single-writer schedule for shared resources
Check for concurrent job overlap before launch
requires-engineering: add distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted visualizations and document transformations, and OpenMetadata is a governance/data-collaboration system that can ingest and surface those outputs. If OpenMetadata treats generated diagrams, extracted metadata, or summaries as authoritative, errors can propagate into lineage or governance records. The verification gap and lack of documented validation make medium the prudent choice.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests next-ai-draw-io outputs without human review
IF generated diagrams or extracted metadata are published as source-of-truth records
mitigations: Require human review before publishing outputs
Mark AI-generated fields as untrusted
Compare one output against the source document
Limit automated downstream actions
requires-engineering: add validation gates before ingestion

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles API keys and broad document types, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory data. If regulated or confidential content from the document-processing side is cataloged or replicated into OpenMetadata, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium fits the documented policy-risk surface.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are imported into OpenMetadata
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Classify one sample dataset before syncing
Exclude secrets from catalog ingestion
Align retention settings for shared data
Document deletion/export handling for both systems
requires-engineering: implement policy-based redaction
